blindSummary:
This country is a member of a regional union with no traveler-facing restrictions on trans visitors, but one of the most hostile social climates inside that union. There is no bathroom law, no border friction for foreign passports, and no criminalisation of gender expression. The union's court of justice is actively hearing a case on this country's refusal to issue ID documents matching a person's lived gender, and the union's free-movement law provides a legal backstop.

The concerns are climate rather than traveler law: the supreme court ruled in 2023 that legal gender recognition is impossible (characterising gender as an unchangeable biological fact); parliament passed an August 2024 law, modelled on a similar foreign statute, banning school-level "propaganda" of non-traditional sexual orientation; and a regional rights-agency survey finds 75% of LGBTIQ people here avoid holding hands in public and 46% avoid certain locations for fear of assault — both far above the union-wide averages (53% and 29%). Hate speech by politicians is routine.

For a visitor: document mismatch carries no legal penalty, police do not target trans expression, and the capital has a small but visible scene. The risk is street hostility if read as trans — verbal harassment is common, physical assault possible but not systematic.
blindOutOfScope: Ethnic-minority issues and asylum-system abuses are out of scope.
blindSourceSummaries: Regional LGBTI-rights organisation's annual review 2025 (covering 2024), chapter on this country: in August 2024 a law banning representation of LGBTI identities in schools was introduced (spearheaded by a nationalist party leader); the country continues rejecting asylum requests by LGBTI people from two other states and unlawfully detains LGBTI asylum-seekers from a conflict region in closed detention; a performer at the capital's Pride event received death threats; an LGBTI youth organisation faced institutional checks.

International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (updated March 2026): same-sex relations decriminalised in 1968; anti-discrimination laws since 2004, expanded in 2015 to cover 'sex change' under 'sex'. But a constitutional marriage-definition provision bans same-sex marriage, and there is no legal gender recognition. A 2023 regional human-rights court judgment (brought by two same-sex couples) found this country in violation of its obligations on non-recognition of same-sex relationships.

A regional union rights agency's LGBTIQ survey country sheet for this country (2024): 75% of LGBTIQ respondents avoid holding hands with a same-sex partner (union-wide: 53%); 46% avoid certain locations for fear of assault (union-wide: 29%); only 27% are open about being LGBTIQ (union-wide: 51%); 28% felt discriminated against at work or looking for work. Indicates a strongly hostile day-to-day climate.

Foreign public broadcaster (Sept 2025): an advocate general of the regional union's court of justice issued a non-binding opinion that this country must not refuse a trans woman ID documents matching her presented sex ('lived gender identity') - the case concerns a trans woman on hormone therapy refused documents; such opinions are followed by the court in roughly two-thirds of cases.

Regional human-rights court analysis blog (Dec 2024) of a line of cases against this country: the original 2020 judgment found a violation of the convention's private-life article over refusal of legal gender recognition; on revision (July 2024) the application was declared inadmissible for abuse of process, but the court confirmed the country remains obliged (under a later judgment) to provide a framework for legal gender recognition - which it still lacks.

International human-rights organisation report (Feb 2015): the country's failure to adequately investigate and prosecute hate crimes fuels fear, discrimination and violence against asylum seekers, migrants, religious minorities and LGBT people; authorities consistently fail to identify bias motivation.

News outlet (June 2011): the 4th capital Pride march passed without incidents under heavy police guard - after far-right extremists marred the 2008 and 2010 parades; only a 'traditional family' NGO protested.
blindLocalsOnly: The LGR ban (supreme court ruling, 2023) and the pending union-court ID case are resident-facing; they signal climate but do not directly restrict a foreign passport holder.
blindTangential: The 2024 "propaganda" law bans promotion of non-traditional sexual orientation in schools — a climate signal; same-sex relationships have no recognition, relevant to trans visitors travelling with partners.
